fix-bug:investigation

INVESTIGATION RESULT
====================
FIXABLE: false

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
This ticket is a synthetic Jira reconciler field-mapping probe, NOT a software defect.

EVIDENCE
--------
1. Title prefix 'FIELD-PROBE-7' is a well-known reconciler probe naming convention from e2e_field_validation_probe.sh
2. Description 'Issuetype asymmetry test' is explicit test-fixture language, not a defect description
3. Author is 'reconciler' (automated system), not a human reporter
4. Tag 'imported:reconciler-bootstrap' confirms creation during reconciler bootstrap probe run
5. Numeric suffix '1780534625' is a PROBE_TS (Unix timestamp) seed used to uniquely identify probe batches
6. No file impact, no reproduction steps, no error description, no bridge alerts, no code_version field
7. The probe script at plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh lines 577-578 and 803-900 explicitly creates Ticket 7 ('FIELD-PROBE-7: issuetype ${PROBE_TS}', 'Issuetype asymmetry test') to test that outbound issuetype changes are intentionally blocked (BY_DESIGN) and that inbound Jira issuetype changes (Bug) do sync locally
8. An identical sibling probe (jira-dig-5281, FIELD-PROBE-2) was already investigated and found FIXABLE: false by the same investigation process — this is the same artifact class
9. The broader reconciler sync commit f4ed5eca23 explicitly identified 'jira-dig-5281..5289' as 'FIELD-PROBE orphan tickets from PRIOR runs' with timestamp 1780534625

ROOT CAUSE
----------
No actionable code defect exists. This ticket is a synthetic probe created by the e2e_field_validation_probe.sh script during a prior reconciler bootstrap run (timestamp batch 1780534625). Its presence in the local ticket tracker is the expected artifact of the inbound reconciler materializing a Jira issue that the probe created and then did not clean up (cleanup Phase 8 either did not run or the probe run was interrupted before cleanup).

FIVE WHYS
---------
1. Why does jira-dig-5282 exist? → The reconciler inbound applier created it from a Jira issue created by the probe script.
2. Why did the probe create a Jira issue with this type? → To test issuetype asymmetry: outbound ticket_type changes should NOT push to Jira; inbound Jira issuetype changes SHOULD sync locally.
3. Why is it still open? → The probe's cleanup phase (Phase 8) did not delete this Jira issue and its local binding before the session ended; the ticket was left as an orphan.
4. Why has it not been cleaned up? → The reconciler sync commit f4ed5eca23 noted these are 'Jira-bound' orphans requiring 'careful handling' due to mass-deletion risks mirroring to live Jira.
5. Why is there no code defect? → Because the probe itself is a test harness; the ticket is the test artifact, not a symptom of broken behavior in the production codebase.

RECOMMENDATION
--------------
No code change required or possible. Ticket should remain open per rule:bug-close-with-code. These probe orphan tickets (jira-dig-5281..5289) are known artifacts from probe batch 1780534625 and require careful manual cleanup involving Jira-side deletion before local deletion to avoid mirroring deletes to live Jira.
